newsitem.title: USA: China's Chen Jian to take part in Korea talks.
newsitem.headline: China's Chen Jian to take part in Korea talks.

text.p: Chinese assistant foreign minister Chen Jian will join counterparts from the United States and North and South Korea at key four-party Korean peace talks next week, the State Department announced Tuesday.
Chen will be the newcomer at the talks opening Aug. 5 in New York. The other three delegation leaders met in sessions earlier this year to set up the four-party negotiations.

They are the U.S. principal deputy assistant secretary for East Asian and Pacific affairs, Charles Kartman, South Korean deputy foreign minister for political affairs Song Young-shik and North Korean vice foreign minister Kim Gye-gwan.
The State Department described next Tuesday's meeting as a preparatory session to fix a date, venue and agenda for a later plenary meeting which will tackle the substance of the issues.
However, since China is taking part for the first time, next week's gathering is being seen as in effect the start of the four-party talks.

The negotiations, first proposed by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam in April 1996, will seek a permanent peace to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Communist North Korea hesitated for more than a year before finally agreeing to the negotiations.
Tuesday's meeting will be held at Columbia University's school of international and public affairs, the State Department said.
